cards.text: Plague after plague has hit Egypt, and Pharaoh, Egypt's king, still won't let Israel go. Now the LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, that He'll bring one more plague on Pharaoh and Egypt. When I say 'one more batch' it's never one, but when God says one more, you can count it.

cards.question: After this one last plague, what does the LORD say Pharaoh will do with Israel?

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses a message for the people. Men and women alike are supposed to go to their neighbors and ask for something.

cards.question: What does the LORD say the people should ask their neighbors for?

cards.text: Walk up to the neighbors and ask for their silver and gold? Friend, I asked a neighbor to borrow a ladder ONE time and got a look that could burn a whole batch. But wait till you hear how the Egyptians take it.

cards.question: The LORD gives the Israelites favor in the sight of the Egyptians.
And Moses himself? He is ___ in Egypt by Pharaoh's officials and by the people

cards.text: Then Moses delivers the LORD's message to Pharaoh, and it's heavy. The LORD says, "About midnight I will go throughout Egypt,"

cards.question: About midnight the LORD will go throughout Egypt. What does Moses say will happen?

answers.text: Every field will turn to dust
Every river will turn to blood

cards.question: Pharaoh's own firstborn will be spared because Pharaoh sits on the throne.

cards.text: From the firstborn of Pharaoh on his throne to the firstborn of the servant girl at the hand mill, even the cattle, nobody is left out. Then a great cry will go out over all of Egypt, one never heard before and never to be heard again.

cards.question: A great cry over all of Egypt. But among all the Israelites, what won't even happen?

answers.text: Not even a dog will snarl
Not even a lamp will go out
Not even a door will creak

cards.question: Moses tells Pharaoh that then he will know the LORD makes a ___ between Egypt and Israel

cards.text: Then Moses tells Pharaoh that all of Pharaoh's officials will come and bow before Moses. Those are the same officials who've been standing next to Pharaoh this whole time.

cards.question: When Pharaoh's officials come and bow before Moses, what will they tell him?

answers.text: Go you and all your people
Stay and keep working for us
Go but leave your flocks here

cards.text: Moses says after that he will depart, and he walks out of Pharaoh's presence hot with anger. HOT, friend, hotter than my ovens, and I never turn those off.

cards.question: Back with Moses, the LORD says that this time Pharaoh will finally listen to him.

cards.text: The LORD says Pharaoh won't listen, so that His wonders may be multiplied in Egypt. Moses and his brother Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let Israel go.
Now, still in the land of Egypt, the LORD speaks to Moses and Aaron. And the first thing He brings up is the calendar.

cards.question: What does the LORD say this month will be for Israel?

answers.text: The first month of their year
The last month of their year
A month of fasting for them

cards.text: New year, new start, and this one won't fizzle out by week two like my resolutions do. Moses and Aaron are to tell the whole congregation that on the tenth day of this month, each man has to pick out something for his family, one per household.

cards.question: On the tenth day of the month, each man must select a ___ for his family, one per household

cards.text: If a household is too small for a whole lamb, they share with the nearest neighbor, based on how many people there are. Like splitting a warehouse club membership with the folks next door.

cards.question: This lamb can't be just any animal from the flock. What does it have to be?

answers.text: The biggest one in the flock

cards.question: The family's lamb can be taken from the sheep or from the goats.

cards.text: They keep the lamb until the fourteenth day of the month. Then, at twilight, the whole assembly of Israel slaughters the animals.

cards.question: Next they take some of the lamb's blood. Where does the LORD say it goes?

answers.text: On the doorframes of their houses
On the altar outside the camp
On the horns of their cattle

cards.text: That night they eat the meat roasted over the fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Not raw, not boiled in water, only roasted, head and legs and inner parts too.

cards.question: None of the meat can be left until ___ and any part left over must be ___ before then

cards.text: No leftovers, which is a rough rule for a baker who's had a cookie in his apron pocket since who knows when. And they eat fully dressed for travel, sandals on their feet, staff in hand.

cards.question: Sandals on and staff in hand at the table. The LORD says they are to eat in ___
On that night the LORD will strike down every firstborn male in Egypt, and He will also execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt.
Remember the blood on the doorframes? The LORD says it will be a sign. When He sees it, what will He do?

cards.text: And the name He gave this meal, the LORD's Passover, clicks into place: "when I see the blood, I will pass over you." No plague will fall on them to destroy them when He strikes the land of Egypt.
And the LORD isn't done with His instructions. He says this day will be a memorial for Israel, a feast to the LORD.

cards.question: How long are the Israelites supposed to keep celebrating this feast to the LORD?

answers.text: For all the generations to come
Until they reach the new land

cards.text: Then the LORD lays out the Feast of Unleavened Bread: seven days with no leaven anywhere in the house, a sacred assembly on the first day and the seventh, and no work on those days except making the meals. He says to keep it because on this very day He brought Israel's divisions out of Egypt.
Now Moses summons all the elders of Israel and passes it on: "Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb."

cards.question: To brush the blood onto the doorframe, Moses tells the elders to dip something into the basin. What is it?
Once the blood is on the doorframe, Moses says the family can step outside during the night.

cards.text: Moses says that when the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He'll see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and pass over that doorway.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will not allow the ___ to enter their houses and strike them down
Moses says that when they enter the ___ the LORD will give them as He promised, they are to keep this service

cards.text: Moses says one day their children will ask, "What does this service mean to you?" Sounds just like my little Chip, asking me for one more story every night after the kitchen went dark.

cards.question: When their children ask what this service means, what does Moses say they should answer?

answers.text: It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD
It is the feast of the first harvest
It is a day to honor their fathers

cards.text: That's the answer they'll give their kids one day: the LORD passed over Israel's houses in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians, and He spared their homes. And when Moses is done speaking, the people respond.

cards.question: After Moses tells the elders all of this, how do the people respond?

answers.text: They ask Moses for a sign

cards.question: The Israelites go and do just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.

cards.text: Hang onto your sandals, friend, because this story isn't done.
